memory.note: Verified 2026-09-05 on this machine: `kimi --help` lists `--add-dir <dir>` (repeatable), `-m/--model`, `--auto` (Never Ask mode) and `-y/--yolo`, and describes `-c` as continuing 'the previous session for the working directory'. ~/.kimi-code/sessions holds wd_<basename>_<hash> directories and ~/.kimi-code/session_index.jsonl records a workDir per session, so the key is the cwd.

attention_patterns.message: Kimi has hit its rolling usage limit for this account. Nothing is broken and there is nothing to fix — wait for the window to roll over, or move this agent to another provider with `failover`.
attention_patterns.note: Observed inline in a live kimi pane 2026-09-09: `Error: [provider.auth_error] 403 You've reached your 5-hour usage limit.` Anchored on the FRAGMENT, never the whole string: `[provider.auth_error]` would be dropped from tmuxFailureTrigger (the format parser eats `{`, `}` and `:`) and the pattern would then never fire on the subscription path at all. The fragment also survives withoutPaths, which blanks whitespace-delimited tokens containing `/` — `5-hour` has none.

bootstrap_message: Read {{bootstrap_file}} and follow it exactly. Reply with the single word READY once you have read it and every skill it lists.
notes: --auto is Never Ask mode; -y/--yolo is the milder Ask When Needed. auto_approve uses --auto because the launcher cannot answer a prompt.
